issues.display_title: Issue #2927: [Fullscreen][Slicing] Build pages-new/fullscreen UI — layout, controls, tray & action rail
issues.main_description_html:
Module

[Module] 18. Fullscreen · Type: Slicing

Context

Build the new fullscreen page UI at src/app/pages-new/fullscreen/ (does not exist yet), migrating visual/interaction parity from src/app/pages-old/fullscreen/ using the Hybrid Incremental Parity approach. This task covers all front-end / layout (slicing) work; data & behavior wiring is tracked in the companion Integration task.

Source: brainstorming doc docs/05-06-26/brainstorming/2026-06-05-fullscreen.md

Scope (UI / Slicing)

  • Slice A — Page scaffold + routing + overlay layout shell
    • Standalone FullscreenComponent in pages-new/fullscreen + route
    • Overlay regions: overlay-top-left (back), overlay-right-rail, overlay-bottom-left, overlay-bottom-center
  • Slice B — Bottom control bar UI: zoom / filter / aspect-ratio controls
  • Slice C (UI) — Multiple panorama tray + show/hide toggle (hideMultiple, showRange, listDataMultiple rendering)
  • Slice E (UI) — Right vertical action rail + bottom-left profile/user card

Target Parity

panorama immersive · top-left back · right action rail · bottom-left profile card · bottom control bar · multiple tray + toggle.

Out of Scope

Data loading, state sync, prev/next behavior, social/menu action wiring (see Integration task).

Definition of Done

  • pages-new/fullscreen renders the immersive panorama shell with all overlays matching the target screenshot.
  • Controls/tray/rail are interactive (emit events / local toggles).
  • No legacy alert placeholders; lint/build pass for the change scope.

issues.display_title: Issue #3014: Integrate List Affiliate API — GET affiliate/list
issues.main_description_html:
Integrate List Affiliate API — GET affiliate/list

Integrate the list affiliate endpoint on the settings/affiliate-list page.

Source: docs/brainstorming/2026-06-15-affiliate-settings-integration.md

Scope

  • Endpoint: GET affiliate/list (base baseURLGo) via FatchApiService
  • Params: limit=100, page=1, search=''
  • Headers: authorization, ec: true
  • Encrypted response → runDecryption() → data.data_affiliate[]
  • Map to UI model via mapApiToAffiliateItem()
  • Server-side search, 300ms debounce + distinctUntilChanged
  • State signals: affiliates, loading, error (skeleton, empty, error+retry)

🧪 Testing Scenario (for tester)

  1. Open /settings/affiliate-list → list loads and decrypts, cards render with correct data.
  2. On initial load → 3 skeleton cards appear.
  3. Type in the search box → request waits ~300ms (debounce), results filter server-side.
  4. Search with no match → Empty state shows ("No affiliates found").
  5. Disconnect network / API error → Error state + Retry button; click Retry → list reloads.
  6. Verify category_id 1/2/3 maps to the correct label & icon (Tickets/Hotels/Flights).

Demo by developer

screen-capture.27.webm

QA Summary - 2026-08-26

Verdict

Bug confirmed by source review. API failures are converted to an empty array before the component can set its error signal. This prevents the required Error + Retry state and can falsely present an API failure as an empty affiliate list.

Result Summary

Area Expected Actual Status
API error handling An affiliate/list failure reaches the component error handler and renders Error + Retry fetchAffiliates() catches every error and returns of([]) Bug
Empty state semantics Empty state represents a successful response with no matches A failed request is indistinguishable from an empty response Bug
Retry Retry is offered on API failure error() is not set for a request failure, so the Retry UI branch is unreachable Bug
Real-data runtime Verify list/search on Dev Not executed after the coding defect was confirmed; no persistent tester mutation was needed Not executed

Code Review

File Evidence Assessment
src/app/pages/settings/affiliate-list/affiliate.service.ts fetchAffiliates() uses catchError(... return of([])). Swallows the original request failure.
src/app/pages/settings/affiliate-list/affiliate.service.ts loadAffiliates() only sets error in its subscription error callback. That callback cannot run after the service replaces errors with [].
src/app/pages/settings/affiliate-list/affiliate-list.component.html Error + Retry is conditional on error(). Required UI is unreachable for the caught API failures.

Test Method Coverage

Method Evidence Result
White-box Error propagation traced from FatchApiService call through service state to template condition. Confirms the defect.
Gray-box Request failure is the state boundary under review; no live request was issued after source proof. Runtime verification pending.
Black-box The specified Error + Retry UI path was reviewed against its source state condition. Cannot be reached when service converts failure to empty data.
Confusion matrix Binary classification: successful-empty vs request-failure. FN: a real request failure is classified as empty; TP/TN/FP not executed.

Reproduction

  1. Open /settings/affiliate-list with an API failure (for example, unavailable network or failing affiliate/list).
  2. fetchAffiliates() catches the error and emits an empty array.
  3. loadAffiliates() receives next([]) instead of an error.
  4. The page follows the empty-list path; the required Error + Retry state does not render.

Fix Direction

Allow the request error to propagate to loadAffiliates() (or set the service error signal inside catchError and rethrow). Preserve [] only for a successful decrypted response whose data_affiliate is genuinely empty.

Runtime Evidence

The capture is intentionally published as-is: the Dev affiliate-list page is visible, but the tester session is shown the login modal and the sanitized browser request to �ffiliate/list returned 401. This is an authentication/deployment blocker, not the coding bug reported above.

issues.display_title: Issue #3038: Integrate Notification follow New Layout
issues.main_description_html:
🔌 Integrate — Notification User

Wire the User notifications (follow/mention) to the backend in the new pages-new notification flow.

Pairs with the layout task Create Notification User New Layout (#3032).

Scope

  • Fetch user-type notifications via a facade/service; decrypt + map; render with pagination; mark-as-read; follow-back / view-profile actions. No BehaviorSubject, no any.

🧪 Test scenario (for QA)

Pre: open Notifications.

  1. Load — user notifications fetch and render (actor, action, action button, time).
  2. Pagination — scroll/load more appends without duplicates.
  3. Action — follow-back / view-profile fires the right request / navigation; button state updates.
  4. Read — marking read updates state + count.
  5. Empty/error — empty state when none; network fail → clear message.

Acceptance: notifications fetched via facade; action + read + pagination; empty/error handled; no any.

Demo by developer

notification-following.webm

QA Summary - 2026-08-26

Verdict

Bug confirmed by source review. The current Follow notification row does not implement the required per-row action control. Runtime Dev authentication failed with 401, so live API-dependent cases are recorded as blocked rather than treated as coding-bug evidence.

Scope and Result Summary

Area Expected Result Status
Follow notification layout shell Notification modal and Following category are available Rendered on dev.panorra.com in isolated Chrome evidence Pass
Per-row action A Follow-back or View-profile control renders on each user-notification row No action control exists in the row template; the whole row only navigates to profile Bug
Read/unread visual state Read and unread rows are visually distinct Font weight and unread dot are implemented in the template Source pass
Load user notifications Fetch and render real user notifications GET /v2/notification/lists?type=follow&limit=10&page=1 returned 401 in Dev Blocked: authentication/deployment
Pagination and de-duplication Append page results without duplicates Cannot verify with no authenticated fixture; source appends responses and has no duplicate guard Blocked / review risk
Mark as read Update the item and count Current code calls category-level read-all; no per-item mark-as-read action is present Bug
Follow-back state Request and button state update No follow-back control or request exists in the Follow row Bug

Code Review

File Review evidence Assessment
src/app/core/notification/following/following.component.html Each notification is one full-row button containing avatar, actor name, body, time, and unread dot. It has no Follow-back/View-profile control. Does not meet the action-control acceptance criterion.
src/app/core/notification/following/following.component.ts linkDerect() only calls router.navigate([username]); it sends no follow or read request. Does not implement follow-back or per-item read.
src/app/core/notification/notification.component.ts Selecting Follow invokes readAllNotifications('follow'). Category-wide read is not a per-item read action/state update.
src/app/core/notification/notification.service.ts Provides list and read-all calls, but no typed per-item mark-read or follow-back API method. Service layer is incomplete for this task scope.

Test Method Coverage

Method Applied evidence Result
Black-box Opened the Dev notification modal in a fresh Chrome QA profile; address bar shows dev.panorra.com. Layout shell rendered; notification data was unavailable because the backend returned 401.
Gray-box Captured sanitized browser network outcomes while opening the Follow category. List and unread endpoints both returned 401; classified as an authentication/deployment blocker.
White-box Traced row template, click handler, category read behavior, and service calls. Confirms missing action controls and per-item read implementation.
Confusion matrix Applied to the binary requirement “row has a required action control.” TP: n/a; TN: n/a; FP: 0; FN: 1 (row exists but lacks action control).

Evidence

Screenshot and video were captured locally in a fresh Chrome QA profile, with the dev.panorra.com address bar visible. The video is H.264, 1920x1080, 20.13 seconds, and decoded successfully.

Real-site video recording (address bar visible):

issue-3038-addressbar-clean.mp4

Reproduction

  1. Sign in to https://dev.panorra.com with a valid user session.
  2. Open Notifications > Following where user notifications exist.
  3. Observe that each notification row has no separate Follow-back or View-profile action control.
  4. Click the row: it navigates to the profile only; no per-item read action occurs.

Environment Limitation

The Dev session reached the UI, but the user-notification list and unread endpoints returned 401. This is not included as a developer coding bug; it prevented live verification of pagination, real follow-back mutation, and read-count updates.
